title: Fixed Four Paddle Shaft and Slotted Board Flax Scutcher
description: One newly authored whole fixed hand-cranked four-paddle flax-scutcher-inspired machine. Two full longitudinal ground skids and complete crossbearers carry two full upright bearing posts, bearing blocks and one horizontal through shaft. Four entire broad blunt wooden paddles radiate from a whole long hub; their full axial widths and separated static positions are visible. A complete tall side board with a true open U notch is rooted to the right skid beside the paddle assembly, with two full diagonal braces. One whole front offset crank, full crankpin, wooden grip and proud shaft collars complete this one machine. No old raised flax-brake jaw, chaff-cutter trough, wheel rim, swept cutting blade or farm frame imported. Unlike the old hinged long-jaw flax brake, this has a radial four-paddle shaft; unlike the chaff cutter it has neither a feed trough nor flywheel rim or narrow swept cutter pair. Greve Museum text supports a hand-cranked four-wooden-blade scutching type; this compact frame and side-board arrangement is a fictional original adaptation, not a reconstruction of a particular museum specimen. One model zero scenes. Static blunt game-art only: no fibre, scutching action, full swept travel clearance, guarding, feed procedure, crop processing, historic dimensional accuracy, force, ergonomic, engineering, fabrication or safety claim. No rigging animation or interaction made.
